description: Compute the compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of any investment, or project a future value from a given CAGR.

faqs.a: CAGR = (end value / start value)^(1/years) - 1. It is the constant yearly rate that would grow the start value into the end value over the period.
It smooths real, bumpy returns into a single average rate. Two investments can have the same CAGR with very different year-to-year volatility.
faqs.q: What does CAGR actually tell me?

faqs.a: Yes — switch to 'Project from CAGR' mode to grow a starting value at any CAGR you enter, for example your historical average.
faqs.q: Can I project a future value from a CAGR?

howto: Choose a mode: compute CAGR, or project from a CAGR.
For CAGR: enter start value, end value and the number of years.
For projection: enter start value, CAGR % and years.
Read the CAGR, total return, doubling time — or the projected future value.
